sources.title: NGSS MS-LS2-3: Develop a model to describe the cycling of matter and flow of energy among living and nonliving parts of an ecosystem
OpenStax Biology 2e, 46.1 Ecology of Ecosystems (fossil fuels)

note.text: Carbon is in every living thing. Plants are where it enters the living world.

steps.title: Photosynthesis
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow from the air into the tree.

note.text: Plants take carbon dioxide from the air and build it into sugar by photosynthesis.
note.remember: Photosynthesis: carbon out of the air.

note.text: Animals get their carbon by eating.

steps.title: Eating
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow from the tree to the rabbit.

note.text: When the rabbit eats plants, carbon in the plant's sugar and other molecules becomes part of the rabbit.

steps.title: Respiration
steps.instruction: Draw the two arrows back up to the air.

note.text: Plants and animals both do respiration, breaking down sugar and releasing carbon dioxide back to the air.
note.remember: Respiration: carbon back into the air.

note.text: Fungi and bacteria are decomposers. They break down dead plants and animals.

steps.title: Decomposition
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow from the decomposers to the air.

note.text: Decomposers release carbon dioxide as they feed, returning the carbon in dead things to the air.

steps.title: Underground
steps.instruction: Draw the ground, the fossil fuel layer and the pipe.

note.text: Coal, oil and gas formed from living things buried long ago. They hold carbon locked away for millions of years.
People burn fossil fuels in power plants, factories and cars.

steps.title: Burning
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow from the chimney to the air.

note.text: Burning releases that carbon as CO2 faster than plants can take it up, so the CO2 in the air is rising.
The oceans are a huge store of carbon.

steps.title: Ocean exchange
steps.instruction: Draw the arrows between the air and the ocean.

note.text: Carbon dioxide passes back and forth between the air and the ocean's water.

steps.title: Name the processes
steps.instruction: Pick the process for each numbered arrow.

targets.role: Takes CO2 out of the air.

mistakes.Respiration: Respiration puts CO2 into the air. This arrow takes it out: photosynthesis.

targets.role: Puts CO2 back into the air.
Passes carbon along a food chain.

steps.title: Matter is conserved
steps.question: A carbon atom is in the air. Which path could bring it back to the air?

options.feedback: Yes. The atom is never destroyed: it moves between living and nonliving parts of the ecosystem.

options.text: It's used up by the tree and gone forever
options.feedback: Atoms aren't used up. The carbon cycles back to the air.
That's one way, but respiration and decomposition return carbon all the time.
Respiration, decomposition and burning all return carbon to the air.

steps.title: Predict
steps.question: A large forest is cut down and burned. What happens to the carbon dioxide in the air?

options.text: It goes up: burning adds CO2, and fewer trees take it out
options.feedback: Right. Both arrows change: more carbon goes in and less comes out.
Fewer trees means less photosynthesis, and burning adds CO2. So it rises.
Look at the arrows. Burning adds CO2 and fewer trees take it out.
The ocean still exchanges CO2. The air's CO2 still rises.
